mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen monotonically over the last four weeks (5.3 to 10.0), indicating households are increasingly staying home. This entrenched home-stay pattern mechanically suppresses discretionary retail and recreation trips, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks relative to the prior period.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is higher than its 28-day backward mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise or hold at elevated levels (>8 points).

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility falls below -25 points from baseline, this signals active enforcement of work-from-home or capacity restrictions consistent with a tightening policy regime, which spills over into reduced retail footfall as commuting-linked shopping trips disappear, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -25 points from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES remains below -25 points, falsifying the spillover linkage.

mechanism_narrative: Joint declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduce the overall volume of out-of-home trip chains that typically combine commuting with retail stops; when both series fall together week-on-week, the compounded reduction in trip-chaining opportunities drives a steeper and more persistent decline in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict, over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES declined from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean rises or matches the backward mean even when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline simultaneously over at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime (evidenced by synchronized declines in PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES and rising RESIDENTIAL), outdoor and leisure-linked mobility measured by PARKS acts as a leading indicator for retail recreation activity; continued PARKS suppression in this regime predicts further near-term RETAIL_REC decline within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -31.1 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL rose to 10.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week despite PARKS remaining below -25 and RESIDENTIAL above 8, indicating the regime-conditional linkage does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week RETAIL_REC series shows an alternating pattern (-26.3, -35.3, -30.1, -35.6) consistent with a short-cycle mean-reverting oscillation possibly tied to weekly or biweekly administrative cycles; this oscillation implies a rebound toward the less negative local mean is due within one week, pulling the next-period average higher than the most recent trough.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC posts two consecutive weeks of decline exceeding 5 points combined
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC alternates between roughly -26 to -35 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays at its trough value for more than one additional week after a two-week decline, rejecting the oscillation/mean-reversion mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Once RESIDENTIAL mobility sustains above 9 points for two consecutive weeks, it reflects an entrenched behavioral shift toward home-based living rather than a transient fluctuation; this entrenchment predicts continued suppression of RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks as behavioral habits resist quick reversal.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 9 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL = 9.1 at t-2w and 10.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean exceeds the backward 28-day mean even though RESIDENTIAL stays above 9 points throughout the forward window.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed comparatively stable and near baseline (-7.6 to 3.9) while RETAIL_REC has fallen sharply, indicating selective suppression where essential shopping is preserved but discretionary retail is cut; this divergence pattern is expected to persist, keeping RETAIL_REC low relative to GROCERY_PHARM over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranges -7.6 to 3.9 vs RETAIL_REC ranges -26.3 to -35.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC converges toward GROCERY_PHARM's near-baseline level within two weeks, closing the gap by more than 15 points, contradicting the persistent-divergence claim.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling TRANSIT and rising RESIDENTIAL signals active restriction of movement consistent with policy-driven mobility suppression; when both signals move in opposite directions simultaneously (TRANSIT down, RESIDENTIAL up) beyond a joint threshold, it indicates escalating restriction severity that compounds to drive RETAIL_REC further down over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell to -23.4 while RESIDENTIAL rose to 10.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean is higher than its backward mean despite TRANSIT remaining below -20 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above 8 throughout the forward window.
